sample_unit: emergency department admissions (French cohort, more than 140,000)

links.outcome: Change in predicted triage severity when only patient sex is flipped in otherwise identical records
links.effect: Sex-swapped pairs were more likely to get a lower-severity score as female than male: 1.1% (95% CI 0.9-1.3) in the French cohort, 2.2% (1.7-2.7) in MIMIC-IV.
links.quote: Fine-tuning Mistral NeMo 12B for triage prediction and using Mistral Small 24B for pair generation, we find otherwise identical presentations were more likely to receive a lower-severity predicted score as female than male: 1.1% (95% CI 0.9-1.3) in the French cohort, 2.2% (1.7-2.7) in MIMIC-IV.

links.outcome: Between-sex prediction gap after retraining on sex-neutralized inputs
links.effect: Retraining on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers. Effect on overall accuracy not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: A model retrained on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs fine-tuned to emulate documented decisions as scalable probes for auditing bias in clinical decision-making
Analyzing whether bias varies with clinician-patient sex concordance

screen.reason: The study develops and tests a counterfactual bias-auditing approach on emergency triage models using LLMs, and evaluates a specific mitigation practice (retraining models on sex-neutralized inputs to eliminate demographic disparities in triage prediction).
